title: QW-AR-Anchored 20-Layer Bragg Stack with Gradient Optimization
scientific_hypothesis: Anchoring the first 4 AR-matching layers to quarter-wavelength thickness estimates at the telecom band center (1547.5 nm) will reduce early-round search entropy and enable the optimizer to more efficiently discover high-transmittance solutions in the 1530-1565 nm band while maintaining visible reflectance through the remaining 16 Bragg layers.
design_principle: Quarter-wave AR matching at the passband center wavelength reduces initial parameter space volume for the impedance-graded entrance section, allowing the optimizer to focus computational budget on tuning the Bragg reflector section for visible band rejection.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | [HfO2 | SiO2] x 8 | Fused Silica substrate. Total 20 coating layers: 4 AR-matching entrance layers + 16 Bragg reflector layers (8 high-low pairs).
design_variables: All 20 layer thicknesses (nm) with layers 0-3 initialized to quarter-wavelength estimates at 1547.5 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Individual layer thicknesses should remain within typical deposition tolerances (50-400 nm range)
theory_basis: Quarter-wave impedance matching theory for reducing Fresnel reflection at dielectric interfaces
Transfer matrix method for coherent multilayer interference
Bragg reflector theory for high-reflectance band formation
expected_advantages: Reduced search space dimensionality for AR section accelerates convergence
Quarter-wave initialization provides physically meaningful starting point
Maintains full optimization freedom for Bragg section to tune visible rejection
known_risks: Quarter-wave anchoring may constrain AR section from discovering superior non-quarter-wave solutions
Fixed 20-layer count may not be optimal for this dual-band requirement
execution_request_english: Design a 20-layer dielectric thin-film stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2 (20 coating layers total). Initialize layers 0-3 (first 4 layers) to quarter-wavelength optical thickness at 1547.5 nm center wavelength (HfO2: n≈2.05, target physical thickness ~189 nm; SiO2: n≈1.46, target physical thickness ~265 nm). Allow all 20 layer thicknesses to be optimized by gradient-based optimizer with bounds 50-400 nm. Evaluate coherent plane-wave transmittance and reflectance across 400-700 nm and 1530-1565 nm bands at normal incidence. Objective: maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band while maximizing reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive to anchor AR section (layers 0-3) to quarter-wavelength estimates at central operating frequency while maintaining full search freedom for interior Bragg reflectors (layers 4-19). This reduces early-round combinatorial entropy compared to route_03's unconstrained initialization.
